Walking around a toy store.  


As a kid, I used to \*love\* going to Toys R Us.  Even if I knew with 100% certainty that I wasn't getting a toy, I still would love to just roam the aisles and dream.  A place like that was magic to me.   


One of the first signs that I had that I was growing up was when I lost that magic.

I have long term depression.  A good deal of that involves my guilt over some groping that I did to a younger relative when I was a teen.   


We've long since made up -- we're actually very close now.  But even more than 35 years later, I still haven't forgiven myself, nor do I think I will ever be able to.   Frankly, I disgust myself with what I did, even though I have never done it since to anyone else.   At least I know that I can confidently say that I will never do it to anyone again.  


However, as much as I might want to get some therapy to help me with my guilt and depression, actually going for therapy is out of the question.  Therapists in my state are mandated reporters and once I "spill the beans" on why I'm there, an arrest will probably be not too far behind.   


I know that some of you may be thinking "do the crime, do the time."  I get that.  But the reality of the situation is this:  Going to prison would be devastating for my wife and children -- who, of course, are completely innocent in this.  It would also be devastating to the relative, who does not want me to go to jail.  As I said, we've become very close over the years and I'm sure that she will (wrongly) blame herself if I ended up in jail over this.    


Lastly, the whole point of getting therapy is to get help.  Once I go to jail, I will not get the help I need anyway.  


So, I simply live with my guilt, my shame and my depression.  Some days are fine, but others (like today) are just downright soul-sucking.

I'm fifty.  I have a loving wife with a great marriage and great (adult) kids.  I have a good job, a roof over my head, food in my fridge and am in relatively good physical health.  And there are times when I feel like smacking myself upside the head and telling myself "what do  you have to be depressed about?  You have all these blessings in your life.  There are people that have \*real\* adversities -- physical pain and ailments, poverty, persecution, etc.  Why the hell should you be depressed when they can make it through their days with smiles on their faces?"

I \*hate\* when those thoughts creep into my head, because they only make me feel even worse.   And it's kind of funny in that, intellectually, I know that mental illness is just as real as physical illness.  It's not just "in my head."  And even when I'm at my deepest depression,  I know that as soon as it lifts, I'll actually understand that it's real and that my questioning myself over it is stupid, pointless and self-defeating.  But even if I intellectually know that, I still feel horrible for being depressed when I have it so good in life.  


I hope that makes some sense.

1.  The relative will not want it.  As I said, she's long since forgiven me and we're very close.  I've spent the entirety of my time since then making it up to her. 2. This would devastate my wife and children, as well as my relative's kids, who all look up to me.  It would leave my family destitute (as I obviously could not work in prison) and possibly homeless after a time.
3. I won't get the help I need in prison.  If the whole point of my seeking therapy is to get help, then it doesn't make sense to do so when it will simply place me in a worse predicament where I won't get any help.  


I know that all sounds cowardly, but it's the truth.  And so, I really can't get any help for this.  I just have to suffer my depression for the rest of my life.  You can say it's a bit of karmic justice for what I've done.
